strain localisation in the early stages of crack initiation and crack propagation in an advance disc alloy can be characterised at a sub-micrometer resolution using digital image correlation on secondary γ′ as the speckles, and the transverse strain Ɛyy in the local coordinates of individual slip bands can be used to identify crack initiation and to characterise early crack growth.
Strain localisation during fatigue in an advanced disc Ni-based superalloys can be characterized at the sub-micron level by digital image correlation using secondary γ′ as the speckles.
the local strain field in a slip band is an important factor for fatigue crack initiation and crack propagation in advanced disc alloys.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel methodology to characterise fatigue failure processes at a sub-micrometric level and the identification of the mechanisms and the associated microstructural parameters controlling the processes.
the development of a crystal plasticity model for the prediction of the strain localisation processes and the fatigue failure mechanisms in advanced turbine disc alloys.
the characterisation and modelling of fatigue crack initiation in advanced disc alloys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the strain localisation processes in the advanced disc alloy are similar to those in conventional Ni-based superalloys, but are more pronounced due to the finer grain structure.
the local strain field in a slip band is a key parameter in understanding the fatigue crack initiation process and the associated fracture mechanism.
the crack propagation is a consequence of the strain accumulation at the grain level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the strain accumulation at the grain boundary is a critical parameter for crack initiation and propagation and that the local slip/strain band orientation is a critical parameter to determine the local crack propagation direction.

the strain localisation processes in the early stages of fatigue crack initiation in this advanced Ni-based super alloy are controlled by the interplay between the crystallographic slip and the twin boundary, and that the strain localised along the slip/strained bands can be used to characterise the crack initiation and propagation.
strain localisation is the key to fatigue failure, and the strain localisation process is determined by the crystallography of the material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of SEM-DIC and EBSD can provide a powerful means of characterising fatigue failure processes at the grain level, and can be used to validate and inform crystal plasticity models.
the local strain localisation processes in the vicinity of the crack tip during fatigue crack propagation are very different from those during crack initiation.

strain localisation and crack initiation are strongly influenced by local crystallographic orientation of the slip bands and that the strain localisation and fracture processes can be described by a combination of local strain and local orientation.
